mechanical_state_analysis.summary: The garage door is in an asymmetric, high-energy jammed state caused by a complete unilateral loss of counterbalance tension while the opposing counterbalance line remains fully energized.

energy_distribution.disconnected_cable_side: Zero upward cable tension. The entire weight of this side of the door is acting purely downward due to gravity, pulling the panel down to the floor or jamming against the track radius.
energy_distribution.connected_cable_side: Full spring counterbalance force remains coupled to the bottom bracket. If the door is midway or near the bottom, the counterbalance springs are at or near maximum stored torque/tension.
energy_distribution.door_curtain: Subjected to severe torsional shear (racking). The rigid panels and track rollers became mechanically wedged in the vertical and transitional track sections, converting stored spring energy into static binding friction.

why_the_door_behaved_this_way.opener_disconnect_ineffectiveness: The automatic opener's manual release cord only disconnects the motor carriage from the drawbar/trolley. The opener does not lift the door's dead weight; the counterbalance springs do. Pulling the release cord leaves 100% of the spring energy intact.
why_the_door_behaved_this_way.roller_removal_kickback_mechanism: Because one cable came off, the door was not at equilibrium; it was suspended in place solely by extreme friction caused by racking and roller-to-track binding. The intact cable on the opposite side was pulling upward with hundreds of pounds of force. When the user extracted the roller from the track, the mechanical jam was released. The upward tension on the intact cable instantly yanked that side upward, causing the bottom panel to pivot violently around the remaining points of contact and kick outward/upward into the user.

system_identification_criteria.visual_markers: One or two heavy coil springs mounted directly over a solid or tubular steel shaft centered above the door opening. Springs have cast-aluminum winding cones on one end with two square-head set screws and 1/2-inch radial holes, and stationary cones bolted to a center bearing plate.
system_identification_criteria.behavior: Springs twist around the shaft. Cables wrap around notched aluminum drums keyed and set-screwed to each end of the shaft.

system_identification_criteria.system_type: Enclosed Torsion Springs (e.g., Wayne Dalton TorqueMaster)
system_identification_criteria.visual_markers: Springs are invisible, housed inside an internal hexagonal or round steel tube directly above the header. Cable drums are mounted at the shaft ends, and adjustment/winding is done via a ratcheting gear or socket drive on the end brackets rather than exposed winding cones.
system_identification_criteria.behavior: Internal spring windup; tension cannot be directly unwound with manual winding bars; adjusted via drill/ratchet on end gears.

system_identification_criteria.visual_markers: Coil springs mounted horizontally along and above the horizontal ceiling tracks running back into the room. Connected to the door via a series of pulleys and long cables extending down to the bottom corner brackets.
system_identification_criteria.behavior: Springs stretch linearly as the door closes. High tension when the door is down; near-zero tension when the door is fully raised horizontally overhead.

neutralization_sequence.objective: Arrest all dynamic degrees of freedom before touching any fasteners, rollers, or cables.

steps.method: Attach heavy-duty locking C-clamps or locking pliers (Vise-Grips) tightly to the vertical tracks directly ABOVE and directly BELOW rollers on BOTH sides of the door. This locks the door mechanically in place so it cannot move upward under spring pull or drop downward under gravity.
Place solid wooden blocking (e.g., 2x4 or 4x4 cribbing) or automotive jack stands directly underneath both bottom corners of the door to prevent sudden downward drops if track clamps slip.
Lock a pair of heavy-duty locking pliers onto the torsion shaft with the tool handles wedged firmly against the top header wall. This prevents the shaft from rotating when working on cable drums.

safe_without_releasing_spring_torque: Installing track locking clamps above and below rollers to immobilize the door curtain.
Placing positive support blocking/cribbing beneath the door.
Inspecting cables, drums, tracks, hinges, and rollers for cracking, bending, or fraying without disassembling them.
Re-engaging loose track-to-wall fasteners if the track itself has pulled away from framing, provided the fasteners are not under direct spring/cable shear.
unsafe_and_prohibited_while_springs_are_: Removing or loosening the bottom corner brackets (where lift cables attach). These brackets are under immediate, lethal tension; loosening their bolts can launch the bracket or shear off fingers.
Loosening set screws on the cable drums while the spring has tension on the shaft.
Attempting to pry the derailed cable back onto the drum groove using screwdrivers, pry bars, or bare hands.
Removing any more rollers from tracks while the door has active cable tension on one side.
Attempting to unwind torsion springs using screwdrivers, punches, or ill-fitting rods instead of matched 1/2-inch cold-rolled steel winding bars.

phase_1_controlled_energy_neutralization: Ensure locking pliers are clamped on both tracks and cribbing is under the bottom section.
Use two dedicated, solid 1/2-inch cold-rolled steel winding bars (minimum 18 inches long). Never use screwdrivers, rebar, or hex keys.
Insert the first winding bar fully into the bottom hole of the active winding cone, hold firm upward tension, and loosen the two square-head set screws.
Transfer tension to the bar, insert the second bar into the next hole, and safely unwind the spring quarter-turn by quarter-turn until zero torque remains. Repeat for the second spring if present.
Once spring torque is zero, the torsion shaft spins freely and all stored energy is fully discharged.
phase_2_squaring_and_track_reseating: With tension eliminated, remove track clamps.
Manually lift and align the door sections so the bottom panel sits dead level on the floor or cribbing.
Reseat the popped roller and any other derailed rollers into the track guides.
Re-clamp the tracks immediately above the bottom rollers to hold the squared door stationary on the floor.
phase_3_cable_and_drum_synchronization: Inspect both lift cables for fraying, kinks, or crushed strands. Replace any damaged cable immediately.
Ensure cables are properly anchored to the bottom corner bracket pegs.
Loosen set screws on both cable drums so they rotate freely on the shaft.

Thread the cable neatly into the drum raceway on the first side, wind until taut, slide the drum tight against the end bearing plate, and torque the drum set screws (typically 1.25 to 1.5 turns past contact with the shaft).

Rotate the shaft to tension the opposite drum, seat the opposite cable into its grooves with identical tension, pull the drum against its bearing plate, and tighten its set screws. Both cables must have identical zero-slack tension across the door width.
phase_4_recharging_counterbalance: Clamp locking pliers to the shaft with handles resting against the header to prevent rotation.
Wind the torsion springs upward in the correct direction (indicated by cone color: red cone = right-wound spring on left side; black cone = left-wound spring on right side).
Wind the springs the manufacturer-specified number of quarter-turns (typically 30–32 quarter turns / ~7.5 to 8 full turns for a 7-foot door).
Tighten set screws on winding cones (typically 3/4 to 1 full turn past first contact).
Carefully remove shaft locking pliers, remove track clamps, and test balance manually by raising the door to 3 feet; it should stay suspended without falling or flying open.

phase_1_energy_release: Because extension springs achieve zero tension when the door is fully raised horizontally, clamp tracks securely to prevent rolling, support the door with ladders/tall stands, and carefully raise the door to the fully open horizontal position.
Clamp Vise-Grips on the horizontal tracks immediately below the bottom rollers to lock the door in the fully raised position.
Verify extension springs are relaxed and fully slacked.
phase_2_repair: Re-string the fallen cable over pulleys and ensure safety containment cables inside the springs are intact.
Ensure both cables have identical tension and identical attachment holes on the horizontal track brackets.
Remove clamps and lower the door slowly to verify level alignment.

inspection_and_damage_checklist.check: Look for bent mounting ears, sheared sheet metal, cracked aluminum castings, or stripped lag screws caused by dynamic kickback.
Inspect track flanges for spreading, warping, or twisting where the roller forced its way out. Hammering track flanges flat or replacing damaged sections is required before running rollers.
Check for bent roller stems, cracked nylon or steel wheels, and seized bearings. A bent stem will jam in the hinge sleeve.
Check end hinges (#1, #2, #3, etc.) on the damaged side for cracking or oblong deformation around pivot pins.
Inspect cables for kinks, crushing, or broken wire strands where the cable slipped between the drum and the wall. Inspect aluminum drum grooves for gouging, burrs, or chipped flanges.
Check that the center bearing plate and end bearing plates are securely fastened to framing and that the steel shaft is not bowed or scored.
